63
Norms to meet power needs from non-
conventional energy sources
*201. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to make it obligatory on States to
meet 10 per cent of their total power needs
from non-conventional energy sources; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Defence framework agreement with
various countries
*202. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there are many attempts to
have defence framework agreements with
various countries for the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof including
the military ties, defence framework
agreement, joint exercises, training
programmes formulated with other
countries for the last three years, year-wise,
category-wise and country-wise; and
(c) whether the above military ties are
in accordance with the independent foreign
policy of the country?
Production of bio-diesel under National
Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
†*203. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have been
requested to bring production of bio-diesel
under National Rural Employment
Guarantee Scheme;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have decided
to include the production of bio-diesel
under NREGS after considering the above
matter; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Solar energy plants in the country
†*204. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of NON-
CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of electricity being
generated from solar energy in India;
(b) the places where solar energy plants
have been set up, so far;

Allocation for rural drinking water
plan
†*205. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the State-wise details of the funds
allocated in the current financial year under
the rural drinking water scheme;
(b) the details of norms adopted while
allocating funds under the said scheme;
(c) whether it is a fact that these funds
are not being used properly by some States;
and
(d) if so, whether Government are
considering to constitute any vigilance
group to ensure proper utilisation thereof?
Soldiers killed while fighting
terrorists
*206. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
DEFENCE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of soldiers who laid down
their lives while fighting against terrorists
during the last three years;
(b) whether Government are taking any
appropriate steps to check such terrorist
attacks; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
RTV buses plying in Delhi
*207. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of mini RTV buses plying
at present in Delhi for which permits have
been issued by Transport Directorate of
Delhi Administration;
(b) the fare structure applicable to them;
(c) whether Government are aware that
most of these RTVs are indulged in
overcharging fare as in most cases they do
not ply on DTC routes;
(d) whether any check is exercised on
various irregularities indulged into by them;
(e) if so, the number of cases of
irregularities detected during 2004 and so
far during 2005; and
(f) the details of action taken against
defaulters?
Contract with Reliance Industries by
NTPC
*208. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of POWER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the National Thermal Power
Corporation (NTPC) has entered into a
contract with Reliance Industries for supply
of gas for its 2600 MW gas-based power
plant at Gandhar-Kawas;
(b) whether RIL has sought major
deviations in the contract agreement;
(c) whether these sought for deviations
will have an adverse commercial impact on
NTPC; and
(d) if so, whether Government are
making efforts to enforce the original
contract terms?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

65
FDI in retail market
*209. SHRI V. NARAYANASAMY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Planning
Commission will give detailed presentation
on retail FDI in early 2006 for bringing
more investment in the consumer industry;
and
(b) what are the advantages the farmers
will get by bringing FDI in the retail market?

in rural and urban areas

Effect of India-Sri Lanka FTA on
farmers
1510. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the exports between Sri
Lanka and India, after the Free Trade
Agreement (FTA), had grown
considerably;
(b) if so, the details of spices and copra
trade between both the countries after the
FTA, year-wise and category-wise as on
date;
(c) the details of steps taken to protect
the farmers of spices and copra from price
fall after FTA year-wise and category-wise;
and
(d) the steps taken including conditions
specified to protect the farmers from further
price fall, if any, while implementing,
FTA like South Asian Free Trade
Agreement (SAFTA)?
Indo-Russia bilateral trade and
investment
1511. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Indian and Russian
businessmen enterprises are all set to
develop a new partnership to increase
bilateral trade and investment;
(b) whether according to figures the level
of trade is still far below the potential and
is limited to traditional items;
(c) whether exports from India to Russia
have been exhibiting a downward trend;
(d) if so, what is the outcome of the
summit held between Indian and Russian
trade;
(e) whether any agreement has been
reached; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
344

345
Export of iron ore
†1512. SHRI SURENDRA LATH:
SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
 Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the percentage of iron ore exported
out of total production during the last three
years and thereafter and the amount of
foreign exchange earned from it country-
wise;
(b) whether domestic demand for iron
ore has increased and Government are
unable to meet the domestic demand;
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(d) whether Government propose to
impose a ban on the export of iron ore; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
impact it will cast on domestic iron
industry?
Capital investment in paper industry
1513. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a massive capital
investment will be required for paper
industry in the next few years for its 7.1%
growth;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any technology upgradation
fund similar to textiles is proposed to be
provided for paper industry;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Steps to improve tobacco exports
1514. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has not taken adequate steps to improve
tobacco exports;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
Government is not making Virginia tobacco
grown in Andhra Pradesh competitive for
international export markets;
(c) what are the steps proposed by
Government to increase the export potential
of tobacco from the country; and
(d) the specific plans for the rest of this
fiscal year?
Pre-Hong Kong consultations
1515. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government, in association
with some international organisations has
held pre-Hong Kong Ministerial
consultations with the stakeholders;
(b) if so, the details of events and that
of participants thereof;
(c) whether Government has identified
some issues which emerged out of these
consultations; and
(d) what is the response of Government
to the issues raised by the stakeholders in
these consultations?
Request of Vanaspathi industry
1516. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Vanaspathi industry has
requested that import duty free Vanaspathi
from Sri Lanka should be allowed only
through State Trading Corporation/NAFED;
and
(b) if so, reaction of Government
thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

346
Problems impeding growth of
manufacturing sector
1517. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the National
Manufacturing Competitiveness Council
unveiled a draft strategy to achieve a
manufacturing sector growth of 12% so as
to sustain higher GDP growth rate;
(b) whether the Council has identified
the problems impeding the growth of the
manufacturing sector; and
(c) if so, the details of the areas that
have been identified for immediate
corrective action?
Granite exports to China
1518. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether granite exports are gradually
increasing from Praka
